subject: Mechanical Engineering
title: Excavators: Hydraulic Powerhouses
description: A fast breakdown of Excavators: Hydraulic Powerhouses for builders.

hook.text: An excavator has no gears in its arm. Every motion — boom, stick, bucket, swing — is pure hydraulic power.

buildup.text: Multiple cylinders work together. The boom lifts, the stick reaches, and the bucket curls — all simultaneously.

discovery.text: The operator controls flow to each cylinder independently. Two joysticks manage six or more motions at once.

twist.text: A large excavator pump moves 500 liters per minute at 350 bar. That's over 200 kilowatts of hydraulic power.

climax.text: No other technology matches hydraulics for this job. Electric actuators can't match the power density.

punchline.text: Oil and cylinders move mountains. That's not a metaphor.

quiz.question: Why do excavators use hydraulics instead of electric actuators?
options: Hydraulic systems are cheaper to maintain than electric ones
Hydraulics provide unmatched power density in the compact space needed
Electric actuators cannot operate outdoors in variable weather
